transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-01 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45 minutes | Attendees: Lena, Marcus, Jules (Redwood); Sofia, Evan, Priya, Marcus B. (Orion)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, our AE. We have Marcus and Jules with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sofia Martinez: Hi Lena, doing well, thanks. We're hoping to close procurement next week, so this is a big one.
[00:11] Marcus Nguyen: Quick intro, I'm Marcus, solutions engineer. I'll walk through any technical questions on Dedicated or VPC setup.
[00:16] Dr. Evan Cho: Evan here, CTO. We'll focus on SLA and perf, also how we can onboard in our GCP region.
[00:22] Priya Ramesh: Priya, legal. I'll be the point for MSA/DPA redlines.
[00:27] Marcus Bell: Marcus Bell, security. I'll ask KMS/encryption and SOC2 details.

[02:12] Lena Park: Agenda — review MSA/DPA high level, cover SLAs and pricing, confirm next steps for onboarding. Is that good?
[02:18] Sofia: Yes, that's perfect. Our procurement timeline: board sign off 05/15, we need vendor paperwork done by 05/10 to make it through review.
[02:26] Priya: Legal needs a clean MSA with liability cap language and DPA that meets EU data residency if needed.

[05:03] Marcus N: On the technical side, dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput. For Orion workloads, our recommendation is 2x A10 profiles or a 4-node small cluster depending on concurrency. We have benchmark data, I'll share spreadsheet.
[05:17] Dr. Evan Cho: When you say predictable throughput, what's your P95 latency at 2k token responses?
[05:22] Marcus N: For the A10 profile, P95 around 380-450ms in our tests with quantized models, less for 1k tokens. These are ballpark — I'll attach the detailed runs, but expect network variability.
[05:35] Marcus Bell: Do you have KV cache/ prefix caching to reduce repeated context cost? We have many similar prompts.
[05:41] Marcus N: Yes, we do prefix caching and automatic KV cache; that cut token cost substantially in similar workloads. It's configurable on routing.

[08:00] Priya: On the MSA, we need to discuss indemnity and liability caps. Our standard is cap at 2x annual fees and carveouts for wilful misconduct.
[08:12] Lena: Understood. Our standard cap is 1x annual fees for mid-market; enterprise terms can be negotiated. We can circle on that in the redline — we typically push on insurance proof rather than unlimited liability.
[08:25] Priya: Also request for audit rights and subprocessor list in the DPA. Are you comfortable providing annual SOC 2 and ISO attestation?
[08:33] Jules Kim: Yes, we publish SOC 2 and ISO certs; we'll share links. For subprocessors we maintain a list and provide notice for changes.

[10:50] Sofia: Procurement will need a pricing approval matrix. Can you break out Hosted vs Dedicated cost and a committed discount example?
[10:58] Lena: Absolutely — we'll send a pricing sheet with committed capacity tiers and examples showing unit economics vs hosted up to commits.
[11:05] Dr. Evan Cho: If we go Dedicated, is there an option for VPC peering or private connectivity? We can't route data over public internet for PHI-related traffic.
[11:12] Marcus N: We support VPC peering and private connections for Private deployments; Dedicated can be set up with a private network path. We'll include network diagram.

[14:22] Marcus Bell: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed KMS? We need key control for some datasets.
[14:28] Marcus N: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; HSM can be integrated depending on the deployment. We'll note the supported vendors (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault) but sometimes naming gets fuzzy in transcripts, we'll send the exact docs.

[17:05] Priya: On data residency — we have EU customers. Does your DPA allow selecting region and data egress controls?
[17:12] Lena: Yes, region pinning is available for Private and Dedicated; hosted can be region-scoped but dedicated/private gives stronger guarantees.

[20:40] Sofia: Timeline — procurement wants to know what the onboarding looks like. Can you provide a checklist and SLA turnaround for support?
[20:46] Jules: We'll prepare an onboarding checklist: legal signoff, network connectivity, capacity provision, model validation, load tests, and go-live criteria. Support SLAs differ by plan — Dedicated has business-hours 1-hour escalation and 24/7 for enterprise. We'll include response and resolution targets.

[24:00] Dr. Evan Cho: There might be a requirement for a pen test or security questionnaire. Do you do questionnaires like SIG or have a security pack?
[24:07] Marcus N: We maintain a security pack with SIG-Lite responses and can do a security questionnaire; full pen test could be arranged on a case-by-case basis. We also provide audit logs and trace for requests.

[28:15] Priya: Regarding termination and data return — we need clear clauses for data return or certified deletion and retention windows.
[28:23] Lena: Standard is return or certified deletion within X days; we'll confirm exact days in the DPA (often 30 to 90 days depending on plan). We'll align with your retention needs.

[31:40] Marcus Bell: Are there any export control or compliance flags we should be concerned about with the models?
[31:46] Marcus N: We have vetted model catalog items and can surface models that are restricted; we also allow customers to onboard private models in Private deployments to avoid public catalog concerns.

[35:00] Sofia: For pricing approval, procurement wants an approval note and a one-page summary for finance. Can you provide that?
[35:06] Lena: Yes, we'll produce a one-pager with total cost of ownership comparison (hosted vs dedicated), and recommended committed tier.

[38:12] Priya: A couple of legal-specific asks: limitation on consequential damages, termination for convenience terms, and governing law — we prefer Delaware courts but sometimes require local governance.
[38:23] Lena: We'll flag those in the redline. Typically Redwood prefers CA or Delaware — we'll see if we can be flexible.

[40:50] Marcus N: I'll drop the benchmark spreadsheet and a sample network diagram in the follow-up email. There's a small chance some model names get transcribed weird — e.g., Bedrock vendor names might be garbled; we'll send clear links.

[42:05] Lena: To recap — Redwood to send redlined MSA and DPA, SOC2/ISO links, Dedicated pricing sheet and benchmarks, onboarding checklist, and network diagrams. Orion to review legal and return redlines. We'll aim to have legal redlines back by 2025-05-09 and finalize before 05/15.
[42:18] Sofia: Sounds good. Thank you.
[42:22] Dr. Evan Cho: Thanks all.
[42:25] Priya: Talk soon.
[42:30] Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and artifacts.

End of transcript.
